Series::positive¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::positive() const -> Series
Series& Series::positive_() const

What It Does¶

positive() is unary plus: it returns self unchanged. There is no computation — no sign flip, no clamping, no dtype change. It exists purely for API symmetry with neg(), the way a language’s own unary + operator mirrors unary -.

positive_() is the in-place spelling: it is also a pure no-op, returning a reference to self without touching its storage or bumping its version.

Since neither form has a real out-of-place/in-place mutation to distinguish, both are documented together on this one page rather than split.

Parameters¶

None. This is a zero-argument identity on self.

Returns¶

Series The out-of-place form returns self itself (not a copy) — the identity result of a no-op.

Series& The in-place form returns a reference to self, unmodified.

Gradient¶

Identity is trivially differentiable: d/dx positive(x) = 1. In practice this rarely matters, since positive()/positive_() don’t change anything a real computation would depend on.

Examples¶

Example 1. positive() returns the same values, unchanged.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 2.0});
std::cout << x.positive();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 0, 2]

Example 2. positive_() is a genuine no-op: same values, same object.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 2.0});

auto& ref = x.positive_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 2]
same object: true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Unlike neg(), positive() never changes sign — including for negative values. It is not “absolute value.”

  • Because it’s a true no-op, don’t reach for positive()/positive_() expecting any normalization or validation side effect.

Summary¶

positive() / positive_() are identity no-ops kept for symmetry with neg() / neg_(). Nothing about the values, dtype, or shape changes.

See Also¶

  • Series::neg: the actual sign-flipping counterpart.

  • Series::abs: discards sign entirely, rather than preserving it.
